summary: Re-review of PR #129 focused on orchestrator/src vs docs mismatch. Found 2 critical CI-blocking test failures in pack.test.ts (stale jsonl gitignore assertion at line 67, stale roster count >= 20 at line 11) introduced by this PR's changes to fixLoopGitignore, .gitignore, and agent file deletions. Also found that retro.ts still implements the old learning model (jsonl -> fold into learnings.md with Standing rules/By topic/Recently applied) while the docs now describe promote-then-prune. The stages.ts line 69 fix is correct. The retro.ts/retro.test.ts code-vs-docs gap is a warning, not a blocker for this PR, but the pack.test.ts failures are critical because they fail the orchestrator-test CI gate.

findings.issue: Test asserts fixLoopGitignore output contains '!loop/learnings.jsonl', but this PR changed fixLoopGitignore in scripts/pack-copy.mjs to no longer emit that line. Test fails: 'The input did not match the regular expression /!loop\/learnings\.jsonl/'. This blocks the orchestrator-test CI gate.
findings.fix: Remove the assertion for !loop/learnings.jsonl from the test. The gitignore no longer un-ignores jsonl because the promote-then-prune model does not persist jsonl to version control.

findings.issue: Test asserts filesChecked >= 20, but this PR deleted 18 specialist agent files (backend.md, compliance.md, cost.md, data.md, debugger.md, design-ux.md, devops.md, docs.md, frontend.md, github.md, legal.md, mobile.md, monitor.md, performance.md, release.md), leaving only 9 in agents/. The assertion 'expected a full roster, got 10' fails. This blocks the orchestrator-test CI gate.
findings.fix: Lower the threshold to match the new 8-agent required team (e.g., filesChecked >= 8). The PR intentionally consolidated to the 8 required agents.

findings.issue: retro.ts implements the old learning model: persistHandoffLearnings writes to learnings.jsonl (line 93), foldLearnings folds jsonl entries into learnings.md using Standing rules / By topic / Recently applied sections (lines 127-196), EMPTY_LEDGER (line 5) describes the old format. The docs (learning-loop.md) now describe promote-then-prune: promote each finding to its permanent file (gates.md, .claude/rules/*.md, context/*.md, agents/*.md), then delete the entry. learnings.md should hold only open questions. The code does not crash but silently produces wrong output: it will inject old-format sections (## Standing rules, ### Testing, ## Recently applied) into the new-format learnings.md.
findings.fix: Rewrite foldLearnings to route findings to their permanent files per the routing table in learning-loop.md, and update EMPTY_LEDGER to match the new learnings.md format. This is a significant change best done as a follow-up PR rather than patched into this one.

findings.issue: All tests pass but they validate the old model: they assert Standing rules promotion into learnings.md (lines 144, 163, 181), topic-heading folding (line 95), Recently applied trimming (line 121), and jsonl read/write (lines 43, 69, 256). None of these behaviors match the docs. The tests are internally consistent with retro.ts but inconsistent with learning-loop.md.
findings.fix: When retro.ts is rewritten to match the docs, the tests must be rewritten too. For now they accurately test what the code does, so they are not broken — just testing the wrong contract.

findings.issue: loadLearningsExcerpt extracts '## Standing rules' and '## Recently applied' sections from learnings.md. With the new learnings.md format (only open questions), these sections do not exist. The function falls back to returning the full md text, so it does not crash, but it does not provide the intended curated excerpt either.
findings.fix: Update to extract '## Open Questions' instead, or simply return the full learnings.md since it is now expected to be small.

findings.issue: The stages.ts prompt fix is correct. Line 69 now reads 'Put your learnings in the handoff learnings array (the orchestrator retro promotes them).' This matches learning-loop.md and protocol.md.
findings.fix: No fix needed — this is the correct change.

findings.issue: learnings.jsonl is now gitignored (matched by loop/* with no negation). This is consistent with the promote-then-prune docs (jsonl should not persist across clones). However, retro.ts still writes to it as its primary data store. Until retro.ts is updated, cross-run memory via jsonl is lost on clone — but within a single loop run, the ephemeral jsonl still works for the retro step.
findings.fix: Acceptable as-is for this PR. When retro.ts is rewritten, it should stop using jsonl entirely.

learnings.insight: When docs describe a new model (promote-then-prune) but code still implements the old model (jsonl fold), the tests pass because they test the code, not the docs. The mismatch is invisible to CI.
learnings.action: After rewriting docs to describe a new behavior contract, update the code and tests in the same PR. At minimum, add a test that asserts the new contract (e.g., learnings.md stays in open-questions-only format after a retro run).

learnings.insight: pack.test.ts line 11 hardcodes a roster count (>= 20) that breaks when specialist agents are deleted. The PR deleted 18 agents but did not update the threshold.
learnings.action: When deleting agent files, update all assertions that reference the agent count (pack.test.ts filesChecked threshold).
